text:
alejandra: heads up — deploy-bot reports a slow drift in embeddings throughput on the staged rollout (us-west-2) at 30% traffic. p95 embed latency +320ms. auto-rollback rule would normally trigger. thinking we should suppress auto-rollback because a set of long-running customer eval jobs are in progress and would be disrupted. @tom @chris any objections?

deploy-bot: rollout id=2025.03.14-beta2 -> CANARY_DEGRADED detected. trigger=embedding_p95_regress threshold=200ms. auto-rollback window=4m. suppression_possible=true (owner_request).

tom: i'm okay suppressing if we have a clear manual plan and can force-rollback quickly if it gets worse. what's the eval job list?

nina: product note: 3 customers running long evals: acme-ai, atlas-research, synthlabs. we've already warned acme-ai in pre-release comms that there may be instability in canary.

chris: metrics snapshot: p95=328ms, p50=42ms, error-rate=0.02%, embed_qps down 18%. heatmap shows increased model load on runtime-batchers. suspect batching heuristic regression.

alejandra: proposed plan: 1) suppress auto-rollback now (so we don't flip mid-eval) 2) throttle canary traffic to 5% to reduce impact 3) push alert to SRE to attempt a config toggle for batching heuristic 4) if p95 > 400ms or error-rate > 0.5% => immediate manual rollback.

tom: +1. to suppress, i'll run the command and document in the release ticket. also will pin release notes to "suppressed autorollback - throttling" state.

tom: running:```bash
redwoodctl rollout hold --id 2025.03.14-beta2 --reason "suppress auto-rollback for running customer evals" --owner tom --no-wait
redwoodctl rollout scale --id 2025.03.14-beta2 --region us-west-2 --selector canary-slice --replicas 1
```

deploy-bot: Hold accepted (hold=hold-4421). Traffic scaled: canary -> 5% (approx). Auto-rollback suppressed until hold lifted or threshold breached.

oncall-bot: Emergency change outside window (UTC 18:00). Oncall authorized suppression for owner tom until 1745552000. Reminder: watch for cascades.

chris: will try a quick config change on batcher: toggle `batcher.max_wait_ms` from 15 -> 5 on canary nodes. small risk but lower latency expectation. rolling the flag now to a subset.

alejandra: keep changes minimal. please post the exact commands you run.

chris: command:```yaml
- service: runtime-batcher
  patch: |
    - key: batcher.max_wait_ms
      from: 15
      to: 5
```

chris: flipped on 2 of 4 canary nodes, early telemetry shows p95 drop to 210ms on those nodes, but variance across nodes is high.

nina: i'll tell CS to hold off broad customer comms and only notify the three eval customers that we're throttling canary and monitoring; message drafted.

alejandra: ok. if by +10m we don't see consistent recovery across canary nodes, we rollback. can someone prepare the rollback command and schedule a short comm template?

tom: rollback ready:```bash
redwoodctl rollout revert --id 2025.03.14-beta2 --to v2025.03.13-stable --region us-west-2 --selector canary-slice --reason "embed throughput regression" --notify cs,infra --auto-pin
```

deploy-bot: rollback job queued (rb-99422) — requires manual `confirm` to execute while hold is active.

chris: after 8m the avg p95 across canary nodes is 238ms (improved but above threshold). error-rate stable. one node still at ~410ms.

alejandra: decision: execute rollback to be safe — we can't risk another customer eval failing. tom, please confirm rollback now.

tom: confirming rollback:```bash
redwoodctl rollout confirm --job rb-99422 --owner tom --message "manual rollback per canary instability and long-running evals"
```

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated; traffic cutover in ~70s. status=ROLLING_BACK.

oncall-bot: Oncall notified and acknowledged. change logged as emergency rollback outside change window.

nina: sent targeted notes to acme-ai and atlas-research: short update that we reverted canary due to throughput anomaly and are investigating; offered to requeue their evals once stable.

chris: post-rollback metrics (30s): p95=63ms, p50=35ms, embed_qps back to baseline. kv/cache not implicated. batching heuristic revert required a follow-up.

alejandra: thanks. action items: - chris & runtime team: root cause triage for batching heuristic variance - eng-qa: add a canary test that runs simulated long-eval workloads - product: coordinate re-run window with affected customers - ops: document manual suppression flow and add a deploy-bot flag to require owner-confirm for suppressed autorollback restarts

tom: adding notes to release ticket and marking release as `reverted - suppressed-autorollback`

alejandra: closing thread after 15m of stable metrics. nice one, team. :white_check_mark:
